notes: Identity assessment: supplied candidate is the publisher-formatted primary research article, with matching title Why Won’t You Listen to Me? Measuring Receptiveness to Opposing Views, authors Julia A. Minson, Frances S. Chen, Catherine H. Tinsley, Management Science 66(7):3069–3094 (2020), and DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2019.3362 on its title/citation pages. Canonical text contains the Study 2 methods/results/discussion and article references; no supplied PDF exists to render. No external identity verification performed. Target ambiguity: description identifies the construct, Study 2 identifies the study, and p. 10 does not identify a specific outcome/specification or resolve article-versus-PDF pagination. Candidates retained without selection: primary clustered logistic regression of same-party versus opposite-party senator choices on standardized Receptiveness, Resistance to Change and Perspective Taking: printed b = −0.27, SE = 0.08, z = −3.29, p < 0.01 (p. 3077); model additionally controlling strength of partisanship: printed b = −0.19, SE = 0.08, t = −2.34, p = 0.02 (p. 3078); regression predicting within-participant SD of selected senators’ DW-Nominate scores: printed b = 0.03, SE = 0.01, t = 2.06, p = 0.04 (p. 3079). Also p. 3078 reports receptiveness regressed on strength of partisan identification: printed b = −0.21, SE = 0.05, t = −4.57, p < 0.01; evidence: report being more receptive (b = −0.21, SE = 0.05, ... t = −4.57, p < 0.01). Metric retained as printed b; the source explicitly says predictors were standardized, so do not silently describe these as coefficients per raw scale unit or convert them. No candidate promoted to a verified field. N: recruitment 400 and exclusion 73 are recorded separately; no explicit mutually exclusive final-group counts or critical-model analytic N were identified in the inspected Study 2 sections. No N inferred from df or recruitment-minus-exclusions. Senator-choice observation count is not printed in the critical regression paragraph. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
